title: Cristofano to the Signori of Siena, c. 1431-38 (ASSi Concistoro 2308, nos. 6 and 24), key R4755

steps.what: siena1421: nos. 6 (1,051 signs) and 24 P2 (2,638) transcribed from the DECODE photographs with one sign legend; no. 24 dorse (637) first pass.

siena1421: homophonic anneal (homsolve2), null-aware (homsolve3) and bigram (sylsolve) solvers on nos. 6+24 under Italian, Latin, Catalan and Spanish models; no convergence (-2.9/token), although the solver breaks a synthetic cipher of the same size.
siena1421: fasc. 1 key alphabets compared by eye with the letters; R4755 indexed ('Cifra cum Christofano', Lucca, Piccinino) but not tried on nos. 6/24.
George Lasry, with Claude and the help of ChatGPT Astra: key recovered by cryptanalysis from the ciphertext only (homophonic, nulls, word signs), per his PDF.

George Lasry / ChatGPT Astra: the recovered key matched to the filed key sheet DECODE R4755, 'Cifra cum Christoforo Ghinucci[?]'; both letters deciphered with it (no. 6 and no. 24 P2), sent to Daniel Bourdeau on 14 Oct 2026.
DECODE photographs of R4755 (key), R4795 and R4812 fetched with the cookie; R4755 is the sheet shown in the PDF.

verify.py: our blind transcription decoded with the key read off the sheet by eye agrees with their letters at 69.1% (no. 6) and 69.4% (no. 24); with labels fitted by EM 79.8% / 76.2% one value per label, 90.5% / 88.2% allowing for labels our transcribers merged. Disagreements are our merged labels, not key values.
LM it-cinquecento order 5 per char: our decode -3.53/-3.62 (eye key) and -3.06/-3.34 (EM) against shuffled-key controls of mean -4.77/-4.77 and -4.03/-4.04 (20 runs each).

dorse24.py: the dorse of no. 24 (not in the submitted reading) decoded from our first-pass transcription; closing formula and signature 'Crist[ofa]no ... si racoman[d]a' found, so no. 24 is by the same writer as no. 6. LM -3.42 against a control of -3.96.
Dating checked: Mantua marquisate Sept 1433, Gonzaga to Milan 1438, Albert of Austria King of Hungary Dec 1437: no. 24 fits 1437-38 at least as well as the PDF's 1431-32.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 3689 tokens, 73 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -2.818 per letter; polyphonic: 23% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value. Verdict: not applicable.

Key sheet R4755 re-read: z is the compound 'So' (plain S = o) and 4 = u. Checked on the DECODE image of no. 6 at all three z places (aduertenza, senza avere, Vincenzo). No. 6 rises from 879/941 (93.4%) to 896/939 (95.4%) understood; no. 6 now meets the read bar.

No. 24: each <...> run of the submitted reading retried, longest first, against our transcription's merged-label alternatives (t=o/q/f, c=h/n, 0=a/i, t 0=+o=i, PHI=m/Duca, So=z, 4=u), the it-cinquecento model and the DECODE image of R4812. 23 changes (7 image-checked, 3 z/u key corrections, 13 constrained by context): ghiacciate, dirizare, usciti, Chamerino, famiglio, facto re d'Ongnaria, a Ferrara, two dropped Viniziani word signs and a Duca di Milano. 1,663/2,286 (72.7%) to 1,815/2,279 (79.6%); image-checked and z/u changes alone give 75.2%. The longest runs (carpelaelo..., vannoafonatificas, stanaeecasiscroie) stay unread.

George Lasry's consolidated report of 17 Oct 2026 filed (lasry_report.md, pp. 13-17): 'Solved ciphertext-only (October 2026) by George Lasry with CTTS built-in cryptanalysis, refined by Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra; the filed key R4755 was found to match afterwards'. Credits reconciled with it. The report keeps the 1431-1432 dating and calls no. 24 unsigned; this project's 1437-38 dating and the dorse signature stay, as questions for George.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): George Lasry's submitted readings of nos. 6 and 24 and, as separate files, this project's revised readings, its own decodes and the no. 24 dorse; this project's blind transcriptions (project_attempt/; Lasry's sign transcription is not in the repository); key R4755 as read from the DECODE sheet (key_R4755.tsv).

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): reading_no06_rev.txt and reading_no24_rev.txt read through. No. 6 reads as Italian with scattered ‹...› words (reviewed B); no. 24 has ‹...› runs in most sentences and is relabelled decoded, not read. fraction_read 0.842 -> 0.286 (tokens in the letter that reads).
Re-read b35, no. 24: DECODE R4812 and neighbours R4811, R4813 re-fetched; no attachment, transcription or decipherment; same images as the 14 Oct pass. Kept decoded, not read (blocker illegible).

texts.label: No. 6 (R4795), Cristofano to the Signori of Siena, 19 February [c. 1431-38]: George Lasry's reading, and this project's corrections
texts.summary: Cristofano de Mont[...] to the Signori of Siena, 19 February: Piccinino's men opening the road to Lucca, and Antonio Petrucci's chancellor back from Milan 'senza avere fact[o] nula'. reading_no06.txt is George Lasry's reading as submitted; reading_no06_rev.txt is this project's correction of it (z = So, 4 = u on the key sheet, 14 Oct 2026); decode_no06.txt is this project's own transcription decoded with the key. Lasry's sign transcription is not in the repository; the transcription linked is this project's blind one of 24 Sept.

reading_review.note: reading_no06_rev.txt reads as continuous Italian (the Mirandola lords have written to Lucca; Piccinino began on the 14th to send four hundred to open the road to Lucca; Antonio Petrucci's chancellor came back from Milan with nothing done) with scattered ‹...› words and editorial letter fixes; 896 of 939 decrypted letters understood. Audit grade C refined for no. 6.

texts.label: No. 24 (R4812), Cristofano to the Signori of Siena, [early 1438]: George Lasry's reading, and this project's revision and dorse
texts.summary: A letter from the same Cristofano, signed on its dorse: news of Lucca and Piccinino, the Venetians, the marquis of Mantua 'acordato col Duca di Milano', 'il ducha Alberto, duca d'Isterlic, che è a facto re d'Ongnaria' and the Council 'a Fer[r]ara', which put it in early 1438. reading_no24.txt is George Lasry's reading as submitted; reading_no24_rev.txt is this project's revision (72.7% to 79.6% understood), decode_no24_dorse.txt the dorse, which his reading does not cover.
texts.note: reading_no24_rev.txt: runs of letters not understood in most sentences, 464 of 2,279 letters, plus the dorse not read (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026). Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b35, no24_reread_log.md): DECODE R4812, R4811, R4813 re-fetched, no attachment or decipherment; the images are the same 2248 x 4000 JPEGs the 14 Oct run-by-run pass used, so the doubtful signs stay doubtful. Kept decoded, not read (0.167); blocker illegible.

human: George Lasry recovered the key ciphertext-only with CTTS's built-in cryptanalysis, refined by Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra; the filed key R4755 was found to match afterwards (consolidated report, 17 Oct 2026; his PDF of 14 Oct 2026 had said 'with Claude and the help of ChatGPT Astra'). This project verified it on its own blind transcription and decoded the dorse of no. 24.
